questions.prompt: How much faster are bitset operations than a boolean array, per the module, and why?
questions.back: About 32 to 64 times. One machine instruction processes a whole word of bits.
questions.why: So an O(N^2) loop of bit operations can become O(N^2 / 64).

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, (Optional) Bitsets, section Tutorial

questions.prompt: School Excursion: find all reachable subset sums of component sizes up to 10^5. What is the bitset step per size t?
questions.why: Shifting by t adds t to every sum already reachable. OR keeps the old sums too.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, (Optional) Bitsets, section Full Solution, School Excursion

questions.prompt: Why can't the Cowpatibility bitset solution store all N bitsets of N bits at once for N = 50000?
questions.back: 50000^2 bits is about 312.5*10^6 bytes, over the 256 MB limit. The module halves memory by building half the bitsets at a time.
questions.why: The trade is a small time increase for half the memory.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, (Optional) Bitsets, section Cowpatibility (Gold)

questions.prompt: When does divide and conquer DP apply to dp[i][j] = min over k of (dp[i-1][k]+C(k, j))?
questions.back: When the best k is monotone: opt(i, j) <= opt(i, j+1). The quadrangle inequality on C is a common sufficient condition.
questions.why: Then each layer is solved in O(n log n), O(m n log n) in all.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Divide & Conquer, DP, section Overview

questions.prompt: How does divide and conquer DP compute one layer?
choices: Solve the middle j by scanning k in [optL, optR], then recurse left with [optL, opt(mid)] and right with [opt(mid), optR]
Scan every k for every j
questions.why: Each recursion level scans O(n) values of k in total, and there are O(log n) levels.

ref.label: cp-algorithms, Divide and Conquer DP

questions.prompt: What is the running time of divide and conquer DP with m layers over n positions?
questions.back: O(m n log n), down from O(m n^2).
questions.why: Each layer has O(log n) recursion levels with O(n) work per level.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Divide & Conquer, DP, section Overview

questions.why: The submasks of 5 are 0, 1, 4, 5, so 3+1+5+9 = 18.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Sum over Subsets DP, section Sum over Subsets Problem

questions.prompt: Enumerating every submask of every mask of N = 10 bits takes how many steps in total?
questions.why: Each bit is in both masks, only the outer mask, or neither, so 3^10 = 59049 steps. SOS DP needs only N*2^N = 10240.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Sum over Subsets DP, section Optimized Solution: Iterating Over Submasks

questions.prompt: What is the SOS DP loop, and what does it cost?
questions.back: For each bit i, for each mask x with bit i set, add f[x ^ (1 << i)] into f[x]. After all bits, f[x] is the sum over submasks of x. O(N 2^N).
questions.why: It is an N-dimensional prefix sum over a hypercube of side 2.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Sum over Subsets DP, section SOS DP as N-Dimensional Prefix Sum

questions.prompt: A mixed Platinum problem: path maximum queries on a tree with point updates, N and Q up to 2*10^5. Which Platinum module applies?
questions.why: HLD splits each path into O(log N) contiguous ranges of a segment tree.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Heavy-Light Decomposition, section Properties

questions.prompt: A mixed Platinum problem: dp[i] = min over j < i of (dp[j]+b_j*a_i) with b_j decreasing and a_i increasing. Which Platinum module applies?
questions.why: Each j gives a line with slope b_j and intercept dp[j]. Sorted slopes and queries allow a monotone deque.

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Convex Hull Trick, section Tutorial

questions.prompt: A mixed Platinum problem: count tree paths with exactly k edges, N up to 2*10^5. Which Platinum module applies?
questions.why: Every path passes through the first centroid that splits it. Counting depths per centroid gives O(N log N).

ref.label: USACO Guide Platinum, Centroid Decomposition, section Centroid decomposition

questions.prompt: Creating Strings II: how many different strings can be made from the letters of aabbc?

ref.label: CSES 1715: Creating Strings II

questions.prompt: Counting Necklaces: how many different necklaces of 6 pearls with 2 colors are there, up to rotation?
questions.why: Burnside: (1/6) sum over rotations of 2^gcd(6, r) = (64+2+4+8+4+2) / 6 = 14.

ref.label: CSES 2209: Counting Necklaces

questions.prompt: Throwing Dice: in how many ways can ordered throws of a die sum to 12?
questions.why: The DP f(n) = f(n-1)+...+f(n-6) gives 1936. For n up to 10^18 the same recurrence runs as a 6 by 6 matrix power.

ref.label: CSES 1096: Throwing Dice
